rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Biot–Savart builds magnetic field from current elements. A long wire gives μ0 I /(2π r) in circles, a coil gives μ0 N I /(2R) at its centre, and a long solenoid gives μ0 n I inside. The right-hand grip fixes the direction.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Governing equation for "Biot-Savart law and its applications (straight wire, circ…" — state with units, then use in one numerical.
Long wire: B = μ0 I /(2π r)
Loop centre: B = μ0 N I /(2 R)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ state the rule without its limit → ✅ note when it applies / stops applying.  ·  ❌ no diagram → ✅ add one labelled figure / structured list.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: μ0 / 2π = 2 × 10^−7.  ·  On the axis of a loop, off centre, the field is weaker and still along the axis.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: The Biot–Savart law gives the small field of a current element: it is proportional to I dl sinθ / r^2, and the direction is perpendicular to the element and to the line drawn to the point.  ·  Integrating around a long straight wire gives B = μ0 I /(2π r). The field lines are circles around the wire, given by the right-hand grip. The field falls as 1/r.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Biot–Savart  ·  Straight wire  ·  Coil centre  ·  Solenoid

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Each current element contributes.  ·  A long wire gives circles of field.  ·  A loop's centre field is along the axis.  ·  A solenoid is the stack of loops.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: answer pattern for "Biot-Savart law and its applications (straight wire, circ…": define → method → result. Structure earns the marks on 6–10 mark questions.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: At the centre of a circular loop of one turn, B = μ0 I /(2 R), along the axis. N turns wound together multiply the field by N.  ·  A long solenoid is many circular turns in a row. Inside, the field is μ0 n I, nearly uniform, with n turns per metre. Outside an ideal long solenoid the field is negligible.  ·  μ0 is 4π × 10^−7. The combination μ0 / 2π, used for the straight wire, is 2 × 10^−7. Using μ0 where the formula already contains 2π, or the other way round, is the usual slip.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The wire formula is not the loop formula.  ·  n is turns per metre in the solenoid.  ·  The wire field circles the wire. It is not along it.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Outside an ideal solenoid the field is not μ0 n I.  ·  Match the formula to the shape.  ·  State circles or along the axis.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Write Long wire: B = μ0 I /(2π r) and say what each symbol means.  ·  Mark the known values, then substitute one step at a time.  ·  Finish with the number, the unit, and the direction when the quantity has one.
